title: Split two more linux_configuration scripts, reverting a third
objective: Bring control_from_mobile.sh (415) and setup_periodic_system.sh (408) under the 250-line cap, and establish when a seam should be abandoned rather than forced.
acceptance_criteria: Both entry scripts and both new libs are at most 250 lines.
bash -n and shellcheck pass on every touched file, with no new suppression and no shellcheck disable directive.
setup_periodic_system.sh keeps its top-level invocation block in the entry script: it has no main(), so moving that block into a lib would change when it runs. Only function definitions move.

For any script that cannot be stub-run (setup_periodic_system.sh asks for root at source time), verification is: the source line precedes the first top-level call, and every invoked function is defined exactly once across the entry script and its lib.
No script is executed. Both install systemd units and one requires root.
clean_audio.sh is fully reverted, leaving no partial split and no new lib directory behind, and remains over the cap with the reason recorded.
out_of_scope: Executing any installer or enforcement step.
Untangling clean_audio.sh's cross-file globals, which is a refactor rather than a line-count split.
Changing what any script does when run.
verifier: scratchpad/verify_split.sh for control_from_mobile.sh; for setup_periodic_system.sh, bash -n + shellcheck -x plus grep proving source-before-call and one definition per invoked function; plus pre-commit run --files and the real git commit for jscpd.
